page: Vultr vcg-a40-24c-120g-48vram is a server instance within the Dedicated Metal GPU family. It features an Intel x86_64 architecture with 24 shared vCPUs and 120.0 GB of system memory, yielding 5.0 GB of memory per core. Local storage is provided via a 1400 GB NVMe SSD, and the system includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. Although the server family is designated for dedicated GPUs and lists NVIDIA as the GPU manufacturer, the active GPU count is specified as zero.

No benchmark data is available for this specific configuration, preventing direct quantitative performance comparisons. From a qualitative resource density perspective, the combination of 24 vCPUs, 120.0 GB of RAM, and a 1400 GB NVMe SSD offers a balanced allocation of compute, memory, and high-speed local storage. This profile represents a general-purpose hardware class suitable for workloads requiring moderate-to-high memory capacity and fast storage I/O without dedicated hardware acceleration.

This server configuration is suited for general-purpose workloads, database hosting, web serving, and application backends that benefit from NVMe SSD storage and a 1:5 vCPU-to-RAM ratio. The shared CPU allocation suggests it is best utilized for workloads that do not require sustained, non-shared CPU performance.
